tools.name: find_esim_plans
tools.description: Lists Inbox eSIM data plans for a destination (country, city, region such as Europe, or 'global'), cheapest first, with plan_id, data in GB, validity in days and price in USD. Data only, no phone number; works on unlocked eSIM phones.

tools.name: compare_esim_prices
tools.description: Compares travel eSIM prices for one country across every brand Inbox eSIM reads (about 50), cheapest first, for a size and a trip length. Read only. Each brand's cheapest plan that covers the request, with its price, the date that price was read, whether it needs an app or account, and its page. Inb

tools.name: buy_esim
tools.description: Starts the purchase of one eSIM plan for the customer and returns a payment link. Pay it with the Machine Payments Protocol (HTTP 402, Stripe shared payment token) to complete the order. Before calling, confirm the plan, the price and the email with the customer, and get their agreement to the terms

tools.name: make_esim_cart
tools.description: For a trip to several countries (or several phones): turns 2 to 6 plan_ids from find_esim_plans into one cart link. tools.name: check_esim_device
tools.description: Says whether a phone model is likely to take an eSIM (likely, unlikely or check), from the model name, with how to be sure on the phone itself. Call it before buy_esim when the customer is unsure.

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Where an Inbox eSIM order is (awaiting_payment, preparing, ready_to_install, installed, in_use, ended, refunded, cancelled, with_support), with data used, the end date and the order page. Needs the order number and the email it was bought with.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "buy_esim" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Starts the purchase of one eSIM plan for the customer and returns a payment link. Pay it with the Machine Payments Protocol (HTTP 402, Stripe shared payment tok…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: compare_esim_prices, buy_esim, get_order_status · Private data: buy_esim · Public sink: buy_esim, make_esim_cart, get_order_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: compare_esim_prices, buy_esim, get_order_status · Private data: buy_esim · Public sink: buy_esim, make_esim_cart, get_order_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "buy_esim" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
